title: pace_curve
description: Payload of `stride pace-curve`. The pace-sport twin of `power_curve`: the same hyperbolic model fitted against a mean-max SPEED curve, giving `cs` (critical speed, the sustainable ceiling) and `d_prime` (D', the finite distance capacity above it). UNITS ARE SI AND DO NOT MOVE WITH THE `units` SETTING: `cs` is METRES PER SECOND and `d_prime` is METRES, whether the human screen is rendering min/km or min/mi. `d_prime` is a distance where the power model's `w_prime` is an energy — that is the real difference between the two models, not a renaming. The curve is GRADE-ADJUSTED, so a hilly interval is comparable with a flat one; raw speed would drag `cs` down for whoever runs the most terrain. Sport matching is EXACT here, not by family as `power_curve` matches: a pool swim, an open-water swim and a trail run do not share a speed model. WITH NO SPORT NAMED THE COMMAND REFUSES: `cs` 0, empty `points`, `sport` "" — which means no sport was named, NOT that there is no pace data. The speed ladder is stored for anything with a distance stream, so an unfiltered fit would be mostly rides and would come back at bike speed. `fit_r2` carries the same meaning and the same caveats as in `power_curve` — 1 by construction at exactly two points, 0 when no fit was made, and a quality signal only when `fit_points` is 3. `cs` of 0 is what says there is no fit. `available_sports` lists the sport_types that hold a speed ladder in the window, ordered by how much data each has. It is populated only on the refusal path (no sport named) and empty otherwise — the human screen and this field read one source, so an agent can recover from a refusal without a second call.
